meeting_header:
Date: 2026-04-28 | Time: 15:00-16:02 UTC | Duration: 62m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lina Gomez (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen (Emerald Head of AI), Aaron Li (Emerald Platform Eng), Rachel Kim (Emerald Clinical Ops)
summary: POC scoping focused on quality evaluation plan: define golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring approach, dataset and workload sizing, and timeline for benchmarks. Emerald wants baseline benchmarks on their de-identified clinical notes to validate hallucination rate and structured output fidelity before committing to Dedicated capacity.
topics: Golden prompts and regression test sets
transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro, I'm Samir, AE at Redwood, and Lina our SE will lead the technical bits.
[00:08] Dr. Maya: Hi hi, Maya here, thanks. We really want to nail the quality checks up front - hallucinations are our top worry.
[00:15] Aaron: Aaron here, platform team. We'll be handing over a de-identified notes dump and want to see realistic latency/cost too.
[00:22] Lina: Great, so agenda - define golden prompts, regression sets, the scoring approach, and plan the benchmark runs. We'll talk about workload sizing now.
[00:33] Samir: Quick context - Emerald is evaluating both hosted and Dedicated. Key success criteria you mentioned in the RFP were under 2% hallucination for clinical facts and >=95% structured output fidelity, and avg generation latency under 350 ms for our short prompts, is that still right?
[00:47] Dr. Maya: That's right, though for longer extraction flows we can allow up to 500 ms. The fidelity metric is most important for ops.
[00:55] Aaron: Also cost ceiling per 1k calls - we have internal targets. We want to compare Redwood Dedicated optimized quantized model vs hosted variants.
[01:05] Lina: For the eval plan we'll do three phases: 1) golden prompt set and smoke tests, 2) regression suite over 5k examples, 3) full benchmark with latency/cost and fallbacks. We'll include hallucination checks and schema enforcement tests.
[01:18] Rachel: When you say schema enforcement, do you mean the model must always output JSON with keys X,Y,Z?
[01:22] Lina: Yes, we'll create format checks that validate JSON parseability, field presence, and field-level value checks. We'll run an automated parser that rejects outputs that don't match - those count toward failure rate.
[01:33] Dr. Maya: On hallucination detection - is Redwood's tooling able to run automated factuality checks?
[01:38] Lina: We have an evaluation harness that supports model-vs-golden comparisons, hallucination heuristics, and external knowledge checks. Caveat: some clinical facts require domain-specific matching - we'll ask you to tag ground truth in the dataset.
[01:48] Samir: We'll propose a scoring rubric: weighted metrics, e.g., 40% structured-output fidelity, 30% hallucination rate (lower is better), 20% latency/throughput, 10% cost. We can adjust weights based on your priorities.
[02:05] Aaron: Can you show an example golden prompt?
[02:09] Lina: Sure - sample: "Extract problem list, meds, and allergies from the following clinical note. Return JSON with keys: problems[], medications[], allergies[] and include source offsets." We'll include 30 golden prompts covering short, medium, and long notes.
[02:28] Dr. Maya: How do you handle prefix caching or KV cache? We want repeat calls to be fast for similar prompts.
[02:33] Lina: The runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; that will be part of the throughput tests. Note: sometimes transcriptions say KV cash - we had that in an earlier doc, haha.
[02:46] Samir: For workload sizing, what split do you want? We recommend 70/15/15 train/validation/golden where golden is the gold set of ~200 manually annotated examples; regression set will be ~5k.
[03:00] Rachel: We can provide 10k de-identified notes; tagging 200 golden examples is doable but needs clinician time.
[03:07] Aaron: We'll likely provide 10k, and start with a stratified sample (icu, outpatient, discharge summaries).
[03:15] Lina: Good. For benchmarks we'll run baseline on your infra and on Redwood hosted. If you opt for Dedicated, we'll run additional quantized model runs.
[03:26] Samir: Timeline proposal: send draft eval plan & golden prompts by 2026-05-01, Emerald provides data by 2026-05-06, run benchmarks week of 2026-05-11, review results and scoring by 2026-05-15. Is that OK?
[03:41] Dr. Maya: Sounds reasonable.
[03:44] Aaron: Yes. One question - security: we need SOC2 plus KMS integration for keys. Also SSO/SAML for console.
[03:52] Samir: Redwood supports SOC 2, ISO, SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations in Private and Dedicated modes. We'll attach our security pack.
[04:02] Rachel: Also need to confirm data retention - we can't have PII retained.
[04:07] Lina: For Hosted we have configurable retention and the Private option can be customer-managed in VPC with no logs stored. We'll document the options.
[04:16] Dr. Maya: For scoring - can we get concrete pass/fail thresholds?
[04:20] Samir: Proposal: hallucination <= 2% on golden set, structured output fidelity >= 95% (exact match on required fields), latency P95 < 500ms for long flows. Cost per 1k calls to be under your stated internal cap - we'll quantify after you share the expected call mix.
[04:36] Aaron: About hallucination measurement - our annotators will flag hallucinated facts; are you able to compute per-field hallucination?
[04:43] Lina: Yes, we support per-field and per-entity hallucination metrics; we'll include confusion matrices in the report.
[04:50] Dr. Maya: Regression tests - how often should they run? After model changes?
[04:54] Lina: We'll run the regression suite every time you upgrade a model or change quantization profile; for the POC we'll run weekly during the benchmark phase.
[05:02] Samir: Regarding scoring approach, we'll provide both thresholds and a composite score so that you can see tradeoffs. Example composite: 100 * (0.4* fidelity_score + 0.3*(1-hallucination_rate) + 0.2*latency_score + 0.1*cost_score).
[05:22] Aaron: About automation - can your harness produce a CSV with per-example results and an aggregate dashboard?
[05:27] Lina: Yes, outputs include per-example JSON/CSV, aggregate dashboards with charts, and raw logs for debugging. We'll share a sample report.
[05:37] Rachel: If an output fails schema parse, do you count it as total fail or partial?
[05:41] Lina: Schema parse failure counts as a hard fail for that example; we also log the parse error type to help triage.
[05:50] Dr. Maya: Are hallucinations fuzzy? Some clinical facts are ambiguous - how strict are your match rules?
[05:56] Lina: We'll use tiered matching: exact, normalized (e.g., med name variants), and clinical approximate (enabled for ambiguous items). The golden set will include annotations for which matching tier to apply.
[06:10] Samir: Any blockers on your side for data transfer? Aaron?
[06:13] Aaron: We'll use S3 with temporary credentials; need an SCP and agreement on retention. We'll coordinate with legal.
[06:20] Samir: We'll send S3 presigned upload instructions in the follow-up.
[06:25] Dr. Maya: For the golden prompts, can we include edge cases? e.g., notes with heavy negation.
[06:30] Lina: Absolutely - golden should include negation, family history, lab-heavy notes, and poor OCR-like noise to simulate messy EHRs.
[06:39] Rachel: On model variants, do you recommend a family? We're currently evaluating open models and want to see quantized variants.
[06:46] Lina: We'll recommend a 13B quantized model as a balanced starting point; we'll include a smaller 7B and a higher-quality 34B option in the benchmarks so you can see tradeoffs.
[06:57] Aaron: Will benchmarking also measure cost/throughput on Redwood Dedicated?
[07:00] Samir: Yes, we'll include cost estimates for both hosted and Dedicated. For Dedicated we'll show per-hour amortized cost based on your expected qps.
[07:10] Dr. Maya: Anything else on metrics?
[07:12] Lina: We'll track exact-match, token-level F1, hallucination rate, schema pass rate, latency P50/P95, and cost per 1k requests.
[07:22] Samir: Closing recap: We'll send the draft eval plan and golden prompts, Emerald provides data, we'll run the benchmark week of May 11, produce a report, and then align on Dedicated vs Hosted.
[07:33] Dr. Maya: Thanks, that works.
[07:35] Aaron: Thanks.
[07:36] Rachel: Thanks everyone.
[07:38] Samir: Recap of owners in follow-up, will include security pack and sample report.
[07:44] [End of recording]
notes: Spoke about weighting of metrics; customer prioritizes fidelity and hallucination. Agreed on sample sizes (200 golden, 5k regression). Security and data transfer via S3; need SOC2 docs and KMS details. Redwood to provide benchmark harness and sample outputs. Potential blockers: clinician annotation bandwidth and legal/data retention terms.
questions: What's the acceptable hallucination threshold? (Emerald suggested <=2%)
Who will annotate golden examples and provide tagging tiers?
Which model families should be included in the POC (7B/13B/34B)?
Preferred data transfer method and retention terms?
